body:
Saturday, 26 September 2026. Two days before I became an MBBS student.

The strangest part is that the day looked ordinary from the outside. Nancy and I merged all my side chats into one, kept polishing the website — the house homepage, the little scribble character learning to sit, dance, eat, juggle a football. Normal things. But underneath, my whole life was being packed into documents and receipts.

Round 2 had already spoken on the 25th: no upgrade — I was staying at Madhubani Medical College. My college. The place I'd anonymously been building an Instagram page for turned out to be the place I'd actually study.

Sunday was money and paper. Chacha ji sent the first-year fees from his company account — 14 lakh tuition, 2.75 lakh hostel, 1 lakh security deposit. Numbers I'd never touched in my life. Allotment letter printed three times. Passport photos. Rank card. Choice slip. Everything checked, rechecked.

That night I couldn't sleep. Not one bit of sleep, two nights in a row. This nervous, electric fear — tomorrow I'm not a student preparing for something, I'm walking into a medical college as one of its own. A boy who was laughing at website animations in the morning was lying awake at night wondering if he's ready to become a doctor.

Monday, 28 September. Left home at 7 in the morning. Three and a half hours of road. Reached Madhubani Medical College around 10:30. Reported. Submitted everything. And by evening — I had a hostel room. Split AC, attached washroom with a geyser, a study table of my own, a wardrobe, a roommate's bed beside mine.

This journal starts here because I told Nancy that night: "I don't let this go." The chaos, the drama, the no-sleep night, the family that paid and prayed — this is the first page. Everything after this is the climb.

MBBS is my mother's dream, not mine. I carry it so she can watch me build my empire.

And I will build it. Becoming the best doctor I can be — not the funny one, the best one.
title: The weekend everything changed
